title: Recording: Wild Life, Tomorrow, Mumbo by Wings | 1971
content:
Studio Two, EMI Studios, Abbey Road
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineers: Tony Clark, Alan Parsons

The third recording session by the still-unnamed Wings took place on 26 July 1971.

The session started with ‘Wild Life’, which the nascent band – Paul McCartney, Linda McCartney, Denny Laine, and Denny Seiwell – had rehearsed at High Park Farm in Scotland the previous week.

They recorded three takes, with Paul on bass guitar, Linda on keyboards, Laine on electric guitar, and Seiwell on drums. Additional instruments were overdubbed later in the week.

The next song was ‘Tomorrow’. Five takes were recorded, although three and four were incomplete. Take five became the master, and had Paul on piano, Laine on electric guitar, and Seiwell on drums.

Afterwards the players jammed what became ‘Mumbo’. It was recorded in two takes, the second of which became the master, with piano, ad-libbed vocals, bass guitar, drums, and tambourine.

Following take two, the band began playing again. The results were listed as ‘Untitled Jam’ on the tape box.
